ex: Var köper du dina {kläder}?
exEn: Where do you buy your clothes?
note: Always plural: Kläderna ligger på golvet. One item of clothing is ett plagg.

ex: Ta med en {tröja}, det blir kallt i kväll.
exEn: Bring a sweater, it'll get cold tonight.
note: Used for most tops with sleeves, from a thick sweater to a thin long-sleeved top. A hoodie is en huvtröja.

ex: Ska jag stryka din {skjorta}?
exEn: Shall I iron your shirt?
note: skj is the sj-sound: "sjorta". A shirt with a collar and buttons; a T-shirt is en t-shirt.

ex: Hon köpte en ny {blus} till festen.
exEn: She bought a new blouse for the party.

ex: Det är så varmt, jag går ut i {t-shirt}.
exEn: It's so warm, I'm going out in a T-shirt.
note: Plural t-shirtar, but t-shirts is also very common. Said roughly "ti-sjört".

ex: De här {byxorna} är för korta.
exEn: These pants are too short.
note: Plural in Swedish: ett par byxor = a pair of pants. Shops also use the singular en byxa.

ex: Han går alltid i {jeans}.
exEn: He always wears jeans.
note: Plural: jeansen = the jeans, ett par jeans = a pair of jeans. Gå i = to usually wear.

ex: Barnen springer runt i {shorts} hela sommaren.
exEn: The kids run around in shorts all summer.
note: Plural, as in English: ett par shorts, shortsen = the shorts.

ex: Ska jag ha {kjol} eller byxor i kväll?
exEn: Should I wear a skirt or pants tonight?
note: kj is the tj-sound: "tjol".

ex: Vilken fin {klänning}! Är den ny?
exEn: What a nice dress! Is it new?

ex: Min {jacka} är för tunn för vintern.
exEn: My jacket is too thin for winter.
note: The everyday word for any outdoor jacket or coat: vinterjacka, regnjacka, skidjacka.

ex: Han har en lång svart {rock}.
exEn: He has a long black coat.
note: Also means rock music. A woman's coat is often called en kappa, and a bathrobe is en morgonrock.

ex: Barnen behöver {regnjackor} till förskolan.
exEn: The kids need raincoats for preschool.
note: Rain jacket and rain pants together are regnkläder, a must at Swedish preschools.

ex: Måste man ha {kostym} på bröllopet?
exEn: Do you have to wear a suit to the wedding?
note: Stress on the last syllable: ko-STYM. False friend: a costume is en maskeraddräkt.

ex: Behöver jag ha {slips}?
exEn: Do I need to wear a tie?

ex: Glöm inte att packa rena {underkläder}.
exEn: Don't forget to pack clean underwear.
note: Plural. Single items: kalsonger (men's underpants), trosor (panties), behå (bra).

ex: Ta på dig {pyjamasen}, det är dags att sova.
exEn: Put on your pajamas, it's time to sleep.
note: Singular in Swedish: en pyjamas = one set of pajamas. Stress on ja: py-JA-mas.

ex: Var är min andra {strumpa}?
exEn: Where's my other sock?
note: Wool socks, ullstrumpor, are a Swedish winter essential.

ex: Hur mycket kostade {skorna}?
exEn: How much did the shoes cost?
note: In Swedish homes, shoes come off at the door.

ex: Ta på dig {stövlarna}, det är blött ute.
exEn: Put your boots on, it's wet outside.
note: The e drops in the plural: stövlar. Rubber boots are gummistövlar.

ex: På sommaren går jag i {sandaler}.
exEn: In the summer I wear sandals.
note: Stress on the last syllable: san-DAL.

ex: Glöm inte {gympaskorna}, du har idrott idag!
exEn: Don't forget your sneakers, you have PE today!
note: From gympa (gym class, PE). The g is soft: "jympa". Many Swedes also just say sneakers.

ex: Ta på dig {mössan}, det är minusgrader ute!
exEn: Put your hat on, it's below freezing outside!
note: A soft hat, usually knitted; a hat with a brim is en hatt. Also the white graduation cap: studentmössa.

ex: Mormor har stickat en {halsduk} till mig.
exEn: Grandma knitted a scarf for me.
note: Literally "neck cloth": hals + duk.

ex: Mina {vantar} är alldeles blöta.
exEn: My mittens are completely wet.
note: Vantar are mittens; gloves with fingers are handskar (or fingervantar).

ex: Jag har glömt mina {handskar} på bussen.
exEn: I left my gloves on the bus.
note: The d is silent: "hanske".

ex: Ta av dig {kepsen} vid bordet!
exEn: Take your cap off at the table!

ex: Alla barn måste ha {hatt} eller keps i solen.
exEn: All the kids have to wear a hat or cap in the sun.
note: A hat with a brim. A knitted winter hat is en mössa.

ex: Byxorna är för stora, jag behöver ett {bälte}.
exEn: The pants are too big, I need a belt.
note: Also a seat belt: Ta på dig bältet! = Put on your seat belt!

ex: Kan du hålla min {väska} en stund?
exEn: Can you hold my bag for a moment?
note: General word for a bag: handväska (handbag), resväska (suitcase). A plastic or paper bag is en påse.

ex: Jag har datorn i {ryggsäcken}.
exEn: I have my laptop in my backpack.
note: Literally "back sack": rygg + säck.

ex: Jag har tappat min {plånbok}!
exEn: I've lost my wallet!
note: Irregular plural like bok – böcker: plånböcker.

ex: Jag ser ingenting utan mina {glasögon}.
exEn: I can't see anything without my glasses.
note: Plural: glasögonen = the glasses. Literally "glass eyes".

ex: Har du sett mina {solglasögon}?
exEn: Have you seen my sunglasses?

ex: Jag fick ett fint {smycke} i present.
exEn: I got a nice piece of jewelry as a present.
note: Countable: jewelry in general is smycken (plural).

ex: Vilken vacker {ring}! Är ni förlovade?
exEn: What a beautiful ring! Are you engaged?
note: Also a circle, and the imperative of ringa (to call): Ring mig!

ex: Jag har köpt {örhängen} till min syster.
exEn: I've bought earrings for my sister.
note: Literally "ear hanger": öra + hänge.

ex: Hon fick ett {halsband} i födelsedagspresent.
exEn: She got a necklace for her birthday.
note: Also a dog's collar.

ex: Jag har nycklarna i {fickan}.
exEn: I have the keys in my pocket.
note: Don't mix it up with flicka (girl)!

ex: Vad ska du {ha på dig} på festen?
exEn: What are you going to wear to the party?
note: sig changes with the person: jag har på mig, du har på dig. Stress on på.

ex: {Ta på dig} jackan, vi ska gå nu.
exEn: Put your jacket on, we're leaving now.
note: Irregular like ta: tog, tagit. sig changes with the person: jag tar på mig, du tar på dig.

ex: Du kan {ta av dig} skorna här.
exEn: You can take your shoes off here.
note: Irregular like ta: tog, tagit. Stress on av.

ex: {Klä på dig} nu, vi åker om fem minuter.
exEn: Get dressed now, we're leaving in five minutes.
note: The opposite is klä av sig (to get undressed). Past klädde, supine klätt.

ex: Jag ska bara {byta om} innan vi går.
exEn: I'm just going to change before we go.
note: Only about clothes; byta alone means to swap or exchange. Omklädningsrum = locker room.

ex: {Passar} byxorna, eller vill du ha en större storlek?
exEn: Do the pants fit, or do you want a bigger size?
note: Also: Den färgen passar dig (That color suits you), Passar det på fredag? (Does Friday work?).
